title.narrative: ILO/KGRTC PPDP "Skills for Energy in Southern Africa” (SESA)
ILO/KGRTC PPDP "Skills for Energy in Southern Africa” (SESA)

description.narrative:
Skills for Energy in Southern Africa (SESA) intervention is a Public-Private Development Partnership (PPDP) that enables a transfer of technical skills from international and local energy companies to power engineers, technicians and managers in Southern Africa. Sidas agreement partner is the International Labour Organization (ILO), who is implementing the intervention in partnership with Kafue Gorge Regional Training Centre (KGRTC) in Zambia and Southern Africa Development Community's (SADC). The program spans over four years starting in 2021 hence being finalized in 2024, and has a total funding volume of 38.3 MSEK from the Strategy for Swedens regional development cooperation with Africa.
The focus is on contributing to SDG 7 on universal access to modern energy, by responding to the power industrys needs for skills development in the areas of renewable energy, energy efficiency and regional energy integration, but also to SDG 4 on skills and training, and SDG 8 on sustainable economic growth, productive employment and decent work.
Overall Objective Increase uptake of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy Efficiency (EE) and Regional Energy Integration (REI) interventions in Southern Africa, leading to a more sustainable and low-carbon energy mix.
Specific objectives (Outcomes) Outcome 1: More power engineers, technicians and managers in the SADC region have enhanced technical capacity to apply, manage and promote the latest RE, EE and REI technologies. Outcome 2: KGRTC has built its brand and standing as the regions Centre of Excellence for competitive skills training in RE, EE and REI technologies.

description.narrative:
The reported results reflect implementation up until the end of the program activity period i.e December 2024. The two outcomes and their corresponding outputs are summarized below.
Outcome 1: More power engineers, technicians, and managers in the SADC region have enhanced technical capacity to apply, manage, and promote RE, EE, and REI technologies
Output 1.1: RE/EE/REI Skills Demand and Supply Surveys completed
Skills demand and supply surveys were conducted among energy companies in the region. The surveys identified a growing need for specialized training in off-grid solar system design and installation, financial modelling for renewable energy projects, and industrial energy efficiency. The findings also highlighted demand for increased practical training components alongside theoretical coursework.
According to project staff, the survey results informed the development of key performance indicators and supported KGRTC in shaping a training portfolio aligned with identified market gaps.
Output 1.2: Training portfolio identified based on market analysis
KGRTC identified its desired training portfolio based on the Market Systems Analysis and the RE/EE/REI Skills Demand and Supply Surveys.
Courses were tailored to address critical skills gaps identified during consultations with industry stakeholders and were designed to align with sector requirements. Priority training areas included renewable energy, energy efficiency, and regional energy integration, with focus areas such as solar system design, grid integration, energy management, and financial modelling.
Output 1.3: Partnerships established under the Public-Private Development Partnership (PPDP)
The project established partnerships with public, private, and academic actors to support skills development, curriculum delivery, and access to technical expertise and equipment.
In total, 34 partnerships were established, of which 17 were formalized through nine Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and eight Letters of Commitment (LoCs). Private sector contributions supported training delivery, access to facilities, and equipment for practical learning.
Output 1.4: RE/EE/REI training courses developed and delivered
A total of 28 training courses in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and regional energy integration were developed and delivered. The courses covered both technical and managerial competencies, including solar PV system design and installation, grid integration, financial modelling, energy regulation, and entrepreneurship in sustainable energy.
In total, 1,151 individuals (841 men and 310 women) were trained during the implementation period. Female participation reached 27%, contributing to increased gender inclusion in the energy skills sector.
Marketing and outreach efforts, including the launch of KGRTCs website and eCampus platform, enhanced regional accessibility to training opportunities. A tracer study indicated high satisfaction with the quality and relevance of the training provided.
Outcome 2: KGRTC has strengthened its position as a regional Centre of Excellence for competitive skills training in RE, EE, and REI technologies
Output 2.1: Expanded customer base for training services
KGRTC expanded its customer base among public utilities and private sector actors in the areas of renewable energy, energy efficiency, and regional energy integration.
The KGRTC website became fully operational and recorded approximately 27,000 visits, indicating increased regional visibility. Training participants originated from several countries across the SADC region.
Output 2.2: Differentiation of the training portfolio through digital learning
KGRTC enhanced its service portfolio through the establishment of an eCampus platform with support from ITCILO. The platform supports blended and online learning modalities, and KGRTC staff received mentorship and training in platform use and digital course delivery. Training materials for new courses were uploaded to the platform to support distance learning.
Output 2.3: Quality control and management systems strengthened
Quality Control Systems (QCS) and Quality Management Systems (QMS) were upgraded at KGRTC. Regular quality assurance processes and post-training evaluations were conducted across all training sessions, with consistently high satisfaction ratings reported.
A digital trainee follow-up and monitoring system was established, enabling tracking of graduate outcomes. Through tracer studies and follow-up visits, 158 trainees were reached, with 71% reporting that they had initiated, promoted, or supported RE, EE, or REI initiatives within their organizations or communities.
Output 2.4: Cross-cutting strategies integrated at institutional level
Policies and initiatives supporting gender equality, inclusivity, and sustainability were developed and implemented at KGRTC. A Gender Equality and Diversity Inclusion module was delivered, and staff were trained as gender champions. A participatory Gender Audit and work-planning process resulted in the adoption of a Gender Equality and Diversity Inclusion Policy integrated into training and institutional frameworks.
Accessible training approaches were introduced for persons with disabilities, and environmental sustainability considerations, including renewable energy solutions and solar waste management, were integrated into training content. Engagement with governments, private sector actors, and workers organizations supported the integration of fair labour standards and skills development in the renewable energy sector.
Output 2.5: Strengthened collaboration and communication for RE/EE awareness
Collaboration and communication for renewable energy and energy efficiency awareness were strengthened through partnerships with SACREEE (SADC Centre for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency), universities, private companies, and other stakeholders.
Joint initiatives supported skills development, knowledge sharing, and specialized training in areas such as energy financing and market structures. KGRTC implemented a new communication strategy, upgraded its website and eCampus platform, and expanded outreach through campaigns, social media, conferences, and journalist training. Public awareness activities also included school-based outreach reaching secondary school pupils.
